articles.title: Why Sergei Pavlovich Is Perfect for Alex Pereira #ufc
articles.description: Could Sergei Pavlovich be the perfect opponent for Alex Pereira? Chael Sonnen explains why a fight with a much bigger striker could give Pereira the opportunity to answer some of the biggest questions surrounding his move toward heavyweight. Chael argues that Ciryl Gane’s win over Pereira didn’t expose some mysterious weakness in Alex’s game. Instead, it showed what happens when an elite striker has a significant size advantage. At heavyweight, Pereira could face fighters who can absorb more damage, hit harder, and still possess the striking ability to make the fight dangerous. But that’s exactly why Chael loves the matchup. Pereira has built his career by accepting risk against dangerous opponents. Now he has the opportunity to prove that he can play that same game against the biggest strikers in MMA. And if Pereira beats Pavlovich, Chael believes the next step is obvious: a heavyweight title opportunity. Is Pereira ready to prove that his striking can translate against the biggest men in the UFC? #ChaelSonnen #AlexPereira #SergeiPavlovich #UFC #MMA #UFCHeavyweight #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews

articles.title: Pavlovich versus Alex Pereira. Who wins?
articles.description: DraftKings opened the line on Pavlovich vs Pereira and it is even money. Pereira is technically the underdog, but barely. Chael asks the only question that matters: who SHOULD be the underdog? Stylistically, Chael says this is the perfect fight for Pereira, even though most people would disagree. The one data point everyone has: Pereira has been at heavyweight once, and the size sure looked like the difference that night. Rico Verhoeven told Chael directly that Gane would beat Pereira in kickboxing 9 out of 10 times purely on size, and after the fight, Rico looked right. But is this the same ask? Pavlovich is a bigger man who likes the punches and kicks, and there is a stigma on Pereira right now: the bigger striker who hits like he does is a problem. That is why this fight is perfect, it either proves that theory or stops it in its tracks. Pavlovich carries the momentum. Pereira says it was never about size, it was the illegal shots. Nobody here becomes a wrestler. They are both brawlers, neither is a point fighter. History favors the bigger guy, which is Pavlovich. But it does not feel that way. You tell Chael: who should be the underdog? Chapters: 0:00 - Who should be the underdog? 0:17 - Pereira the underdog, barely; even money 0:28 - Pereira's one heavyweight night: size was the difference 0:46 - Rico Verhoeven: Gane beats Pereira 9/10 in kickboxing 1:14 - Natural heavyweight vs grown heavyweight 1:52 - The stigma: bigger strikers are Pereira's problem 2:05 - Why this is the perfect fight for Pereira 2:12 - Momentum: Pavlovich's last fight is headwind 2:33 - Pereira blames illegal shots, not size 3:05 - Gane hits hard, Pavlovich hits just as hard 3:36 - Pereira is not suddenly becoming a wrestler 3:52 - Who should be favorite? DraftKings has it even 4:06 - If Pereira wins, it is a striking stoppage 4:36 - Two brawlers, no point fighters 5:03 - History favors the bigger guy: Pavlovich 5:23 - DraftKings cannot decide, so you decide: who should be the underdog? #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #Pereira #Pavlovich

articles.title: Chael's Problem with Michael Morales' Promo Video
articles.description: Michael Morales dropped a slick, self-produced promo video, and Chael Sonnen has notes, plus a prediction about what comes next. Chael starts with full credit: the production is top-shelf. Lighting, sound, Morales looking sharp in a suit, a fight-promo feel with real clips. Then he tackles it two ways. First, the production: Morales speaks another language and the music is mixed so loud it's hard to understand him. Chael's fix is simple, turn the music down and let the fighter be heard. Second, the script: Morales said too much and named too many names. Chael's rule is say a third of what you planned. One clear callout, then stop. Then Chael gets into the philosophy. The chicken-and-egg of stardom: you can't become a star without a media push, so how do you get the push? Kevin Lee, Colby Covington, and Henry Cejudo solved it by taking the financial risk and building their own promotional machines. Chael loves that Morales did the same. And the fallout is already here. Shavkat Rakhmonov answered with a TikTok caption hinting at 19-0 versus 19-0, Morales versus Rakhmonov is suddenly very real, and there's a quiet race with Carlos Prates to be next for Islam Makhachev. Chael lays out how the title-race game gets played in the media and by managers, and asks the only question that matters: which fight do you want to see? Chapters: 0:00 - Morales' well-produced Instagram promo video 0:30 - the chicken-and-egg of becoming a star 1:25 - Kevin Lee, Colby Covington, Henry Cejudo built their own promotional machines 2:05 - Chael's one problem: the critique 2:37 - going after Islam is fair play, nobody bullies Islam 2:53 - then Rakhmonov, now the viewer must choose 3:14 - third name: Ian Garry, the middle-finger ending 3:42 - too many names, viewer left choosing between the three 4:49 - Prates/title race, best time to fight Rakhmonov is his return 5:14 - the Ian Garry back-and-forth story 5:38 - final critique: next time, tell me what you want 6:00 - the champ is the one you want, only call out the champ #MMA #UFC #ChaelSonnen #MichaelMorales

articles.title: Does Josh Hokit Deserve Ciryl Gane Fight?
articles.description: Tom Aspinall held the heavyweight title two weeks ago. Now he doesn't, and the whole division is a riddle. Chael sits down with the new rankings and works through the title picture name by name. Ciryl Gane is at the top of the bill, but who gets the first crack at him? Alex Pereira has the most decorated resume in the sport, but he just fought Gane and it wasn't competitive. Aspinall has an eye injury. Volkov makes sense by the numbers, and Chael believes he won the fight against Gane even if he lost the decision, but history says rematches never win out over fresh matchups. Pavlovich lost to Volkov, so he can't survive the elimination either. That leaves Josh Hokit, undefeated in the UFC and undefeated, period. Ariel Helwani says the shot came from everything Hokit brings outside the cage. Chael's answer: name one thing said at a press conference that made him undefeated, that got him Fight of the Night against Curtis Blaydes, that beat Derrick Lewis, that put on a dominant performance at the White House. Nothing did. The record did. Chapters: 0:00 - Ariel's take: Hokit earned his title shot with what he does outside the cage 0:29 - Chael's pushback: is there something Hokit SAID that made him undefeated? 0:59 - the heavyweight title picture is a riddle: Aspinall held it two weeks ago 1:46 - Alex Pereira's decorative resume, but the last fight was not competitive 2:14 - Volkov won the fight but lost the decision; rematches vs fresh blood 2:32 - the mandate of the masses: press conferences, T-shirts, merchandise before a title shot 3:27 - who else would you give it to? Pavlovich's loss to Volkov eliminates him 3:44 - so Hokit IS the right answer, but was it the press conference that got him there? 4:12 - the ambulance stretcher story: he did not ask for that fight 4:26 - maybe it was not the mic skills: X-and-0, nobody has ever beaten him 5:07 - Volkov must make his next fight demand attention from the masses 5:35 - "and he's completely undefeated" #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #Heavyweight

articles.title: Strickland Has TWO Offers... Which Would YOU Take?
articles.description: Sean Strickland wants more money, and two middleweights just made him offers he can't ignore. Chael Sonnen breaks down the wildest contract standoff in the middleweight division: Strickland, the champion, is holding out for bigger pay, and Nassourdine Imavov publicly offered to sweeten his pot by $500,000 if he beats him. Then Khamzat Chimaev doubled it, posting a single lemon emoji the internet decoded as one million dollars, and added they could do it in the gym, in the street, or in the cage. Chael takes both offers literally and asks the only question that matters: which one would you take? Imavov's half million requires a win. Chimaev's million just requires showing up, no sanctioning body needed. And with the December title picture shifting after the latest announcements, the timing of Strickland's next two fights, potentially Imavov then Chimaev, makes both offers live ammunition. Plus: the motorcycle accident rumors, what Strickland confirmed on Instagram, and why the BMF title announcement changed the December main event picture. Chapters: 0:00 - Strickland wants more money 0:30 - "I'll fight Chimaev, but not next" 0:58 - The two-part announcement shakes up December 1:24 - Motorcycle accident or money holdout? 2:03 - Imavov's $500K offer 2:44 - Chimaev's $1M lemon emoji 3:29 - Which offer would you take? 4:06 - Why neither offer expires 6:22 - Chael on Strickland's character 7:06 - January timeline, it will all work out 8:06 - An unwilling champion and the stripped word 9:19 - Chael's prediction: Imavov, then Chimaev #MMA #UFC #SeanStrickland #KhamzatChimaev

articles.title: Why Chael Sonnen was able to talk as much trash as he wanted #ufc
articles.description: Dana White has taken criticism for his leadership, but Chael Sonnen sees one particular decision as a sign of what makes him different: he lets UFC fighters speak for themselves. Chael explains why Dana refuses to dictate what fighters can or cannot say during interviews and promotions. In his view, scripting their words would undermine the authenticity that makes MMA compelling—and turn the UFC into something more like professional wrestling. The conversation touches on Anderson Silva and the consequences of an unscripted moment, while exploring the difference between genuine fighter expression and carefully manufactured promotional content. Chael argues that Dana’s hands-off approach isn’t about politics or being deliberately harsh. It’s about allowing fighters to own their words, even when those words attract criticism. Is letting fighters speak freely a strength of the UFC, or should there be more control over what they say? #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #UFC #MMA #AndersonSilva #UFCPromos #MMAInterviews #FightPromotion #WWE

articles.title: Justin Gaethje’s Retirement Is Now a Real Possibility #ufc
articles.description: Is Justin Gaethje seriously considering retirement? Chael Sonnen says the possibility is now more real than he ever believed. Chael explains why the usual story surrounding Gaethje vs. Arman Tsarukyan doesn't quite fit. There’s no bad blood, no real rivalry, and no personal heat pushing this matchup forward. In fact, Gaethje and Arman respect each other — and that changes the entire dynamic. But the bigger question is what Gaethje actually wants to do next. Chael says he has always assumed Gaethje would fight Arman, fight Ilia Topuria, and continue competing at the highest level. He never really considered the possibility that Gaethje might decide to fight one more time and walk away. Now, he does. Chael breaks down why Gaethje may be in the perfect position to retire on his own terms — and why the decision should ultimately come down to what Justin wants. Is one more UFC fight coming, or could we be watching the final chapter of Justin Gaethje’s career? #ChaelSonnen #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #IliaTopuria #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: This Has to Be a No. 1 Contender Fight for Both Guys #ufc
articles.description: What happens if O’Malley beats Ali and immediately gets a title shot? Chael Sonnen says there’s a problem with that logic — because if this matchup is being treated as a path to the title for O’Malley, it has to mean the same thing for Ali. Chael breaks down why Ali has every right to ask, “What’s in it for me?” The champion wrestler has already shown he can wrestle, strike, and bring a complete skill set into the Octagon. But if Ali believes this fight is his road to a championship opportunity, Chael says he’s completely on board — with one major condition. If this is a No. 1 contender fight, it needs to be a No. 1 contender fight for BOTH men. And there’s another concern: booking one of the sport’s biggest stars against Ali could accidentally turn Ali into a stepping stone. That may not be the intention, but the stakes of the matchup matter. Chael explains why the UFC has to be careful with this fight — and why the winner should have a legitimate path to the title. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #SeanOMalley #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews #UFCMatchmaking #Wrestling

articles.title: Would Chael Fight Anderson Silva Again?
articles.description: It's time for Ask Uncle Chael, and Chael Sonnen answers your questions from across the combat sports world. Chael explains why MMA stars have become so important to Real American Freestyle, names the RAF matchups he most wants to see, and responds to the reaction surrounding Gable Steveson's stunning knockout loss. Does Gable have a glass jaw—or did he simply get caught by a massive shot that would have put anybody down? Chael also gives an update on Mean Street Pizza, reveals whether he'd accept another MMA fight with Anderson Silva, talks about the competitive itch that still comes back around Olympic season, and reminds Francis Ngannou that his arm-wrestling challenge still stands. Plus, Chael discusses the future of an injured UFC fighter, gives an update on Brother Joel and closes by naming some of the greatest coaches in MMA history including Matt Hume, Javier Mendez, Greg Jackson, Mike Winkeljohn and Firas Zahabi. articles.title: Sean Strickland Wants $1 Million to Fight Imavov
articles.description: Sean Strickland vs. Nassourdine Imavov appeared headed for a December showdown in Las Vegas—until a different main event was announced and the rumored middleweight fight disappeared. Now reports suggest money may have gotten in the way, including a claim that Strickland wanted $1 million for the fight. Imavov responded publicly with an offer of his own: he can't give Strickland that money just to show up, but he'll put up $500,000 if Strickland can beat him. Chael Sonnen explains why he doesn't believe the simple solution is moving the same matchup to January. More importantly, what happens to Imavov? He's healthy, willing to compete and sitting in the prime of his career, yet could potentially spend an entire year on the sidelines. Chael breaks down the Strickland situation, Imavov's uncertain position, where Khamzat Chimaev fits into the middleweight picture, and why keeping Imavov inactive could ultimately hurt one of the division's top contenders.

articles.title: Sean O'Malley MUST Accept Talbott's Challenge
articles.description: Payton Talbott called out Sean O'Malley, and Chael Sonnen believes he picked exactly the right name at exactly the right time. Talbott has now beaten two former world champions, and a win over O'Malley would make it extremely difficult to deny him a shot at the bantamweight title. But Chael argues the same opportunity needs to exist for Sean. If O'Malley vs. Talbott is effectively a semifinal, whoever wins should advance—regardless of which fighter the UFC or the audience expected to come out on top. Chael explains why he believes O'Malley will be interested in the matchup, why Talbott brings something to the fight that some of Sean's previous opponents didn't, and why the UFC should make the stakes clear. O'Malley vs. Talbott. Merab Dvalishvili vs. Petr Yan. Chael's proposal is simple: let the winners fight for the bantamweight championship.

articles.title: Alex Pereira vs. Pavlovich Is the PERFECT Fight
articles.description: Alex Pereira vs. Sergei Pavlovich is official, and on paper it looks like one of the worst possible matchups for Pereira. Pavlovich is bigger, he's a dangerous striker, and he's coming off a win while Pereira is coming off the Ciryl Gane loss. That's exactly why Chael Sonnen believes this is the perfect fight for Pereira. The Gane fight raised a major question about Pereira at heavyweight: can the same dangerous striking game that made him a champion at middleweight and light heavyweight work against elite heavyweights who are considerably bigger than him? Pavlovich gives Pereira the opportunity to answer that question immediately and potentially show that what happened against Gane was simply an outlier. Chael breaks down the matchup, why Pereira accepted such a dangerous opponent, and how a victory could put him right back into the heavyweight title conversation alongside Alexander Volkov and the rest of the division. CHAPTERS: 00:00 - Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira is official 00:04 - Pereira's picture with Hunter Campbell: offices are for finalizing, not talking 00:32 - Title-picture chaos: Aspinall situation and how Pereira landed this shot 00:47 - With Almeida taking the Gane job, it's Pereira vs. Pavlovich 01:00 - Why this is the perfect fight for Pereira 01:12 - On paper it sucks: Pavlovich's size, style, coming off a win; Pereira off a KO loss 01:40 - The Gane lesson: a bigger striker kickboxing in MMA gloves, no hidden weakness exposed 02:29 - Pereira can answer every question and prove Gane was an outlier 02:39 - A win puts Pereira right back into a title opportunity (but Volkov qualifies too) 03:37 - "I love the fight": Pereira's massive opportunity 04:01 - The chess perspective: this complicates the entire heavyweight division #AlexPereira #SergeiPavlovich #UFC #MMA #Heavyweight

articles.title: How the UFC cheated Chael Sonnen #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen says he would never have failed a drug test—if he had known the rules in advance. In this candid discussion, Chael revisits the random drug testing that caught him off guard, calling it a “scumbag move” and claiming he could have manipulated the system had the procedures been explained beforehand. He argues that the surprise element was the key issue, while acknowledging that testing itself could continue. The conversation raises questions about the evolution of MMA drug testing, out-of-competition procedures, and the distinction between scheduled and random tests. Chael offers his own perspective on how the system worked at the time and why he believes the rules made a difference. Watch as Chael explains his controversial stance on UFC drug testing and reflects on the circumstances surrounding his suspension. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #DrugTesting #USADA #UFCHistory #MMAControversy #PerformanceEnhancingDrugs

articles.title: Justin Gaethje’s retirement is closer than you think.
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is in Salt Lake City and has heard enough around the UFC to reconsider something he previously didn't believe: Justin Gaethje may genuinely be considering retirement. Chael explains why Gaethje is in a uniquely clean position to walk away. There is no personal rivalry with Arman Tsarukyan, no announced fight, no obvious No. 1 contender waiting on him and no unfinished business forcing his hand. Unlike other retirement situations where a major matchup was already hanging over the champion, Gaethje could leave without ducking anyone or leaving an obvious fight behind. Chael still wants Gaethje to make whatever decision is right for him. But after previously dismissing the retirement talk, he now believes the possibility that Justin Gaethje has fought for the final time is much more real than most fans realize. articles.title: Why O'Malley vs Talbott Has to Happen Next
articles.description: Peyton Talbot just did something almost nobody does: he beat a 135-pound champion and a 125-pound champion, and now he's calling for Sean O'Malley. Chael breaks down why history says beating a world champion earns you a title shot, why beating two makes it undeniable, and why the bantamweight division's search for new blood makes Talbot the perfect candidate. But there's a catch. Talbot didn't ask for a title shot, he asked for O'Malley. And if Talbot vs O'Malley is a number one contender fight for Talbot, it has to be one for O'Malley too. Chael digs into the matchmaking science nobody talks about, what Henry told him after feeling Talbot's level firsthand, and the uncomfortable question O'Malley is finally asking: what's in it for me? articles.title: Daniel Cormier on Alex Pereira NEXT UFC FIGHT announcement: Ulberg, Volkov, Pavlovic, Chimaev?
articles.description: Daniel Cormier IS BACK with a brand new DC Show, this time breaking down UFC superstar Alex Pereira and the potential announcement TODAY of who the heavyweight star will be fighting next. DC believes that his next fight will be at heavyweight, but still feels that Alex would be A PROBLEM at 205 if he was to choose a fight between a top contender or Champion like Carlos Ulberg or Khamzat Chimaev if he chooses to move up a division. DC also speaks on Dana White and the UFC going forward with the Josh Hokit and Ciryl Gane fight, and why he doubles down on that being the fight to make. Plus, DC reacts to Nina Drama and the UFC's viral post about Dana announcing Alex's fight Saturday night around UFC 332, and why he believes the next fight will likely still be at heavyweight.
